problem: State-of-the-art point-goal navigation agents need tens of millions to billions of RL steps because visual representations must be learned purely from sparse task reward, which is very sample-inefficient.
motivation: Extreme training durations limit research accessibility and scalability. The authors hypothesize that the long training is mostly due to the difficulty of learning useful visual representations from task reward alone, so dense auxiliary supervision already available in simulators could speed it up.
key_idea: Add three simulator-supervised auxiliary tasks (local scene geometry, environment transition dynamics, and progress toward the goal) to RL-trained PointNav agents to shape their representations and improve sample efficiency.
insight: Auxiliary losses that target task-relevant elements (geometry, dynamics, goal progress) provide strong supervision that can be evaluated independent of task performance. Applied to prior agents, they yield over 4x sample efficiency, with augmented agents at 17M steps outperforming SOTA agents trained for 72M steps. This suggests much of the training cost is representation learning rather than policy learning. Only the abstract was available, so no ablation detail is known.
method: Local scene geometry auxiliary task: predicts local geometry of the scene from the learned representation, supervised by simulator information.
Transition dynamics auxiliary task: predicts environment transition dynamics (the effect of actions on observations or state) using simulator supervision.
Goal progress auxiliary task: predicts progress toward the point goal.
Plug-in usage: the auxiliary losses are added to agents from prior work alongside the RL objective, using supervision already present in the simulator.

setting.backbone: Prior PointNav RL agents (e.g., DD-PPO-style CNN + RNN policy) augmented with auxiliary heads, trained with RL
setting.training_data: Simulator RL experience in photorealistic environments, 17M steps with auxiliary supervision from the simulator; no external data
setting.observation: egocentric visual observations (likely RGB-D) plus point-goal
setting.privileged: Simulator-derived ground truth used only as training-time auxiliary supervision; none at test time

results: Applying the auxiliary losses to prior-work agents gives over 4x sample efficiency: at 17M steps, augmented agents outperform state-of-the-art agents trained for 72M steps.
limitations: Only PointNav in simulation is evaluated; there is no real-robot evidence.
Auxiliary supervision depends on simulator-provided ground truth (geometry, dynamics, progress).
compares_to: state-of-the-art PointNav agents trained for 72M steps
